_comment: Operator-reachable behaviours DELIBERATELY excluded from the menu-completeness gate. The gate quantifies over BEHAVIOURS, not registry rows — that is what makes it a verifier rather than a tautology, since menus are generated from the registry. Every exclusion below carries a mandatory reason. The gate FAILS CLOSED: a key handled in key_event_to_terminal_input that is neither a registry hotkey nor listed here is a RED BUILD. Adding an entry is a design decision, not a fix — see plan/02-menu-shell-primacy/handoff.md § 3b.
_posture: REGISTER BY DEFAULT (maintainer, 2026-08-03). Exclusion is the exception and must be argued. If a behaviour could plausibly sit in a menu, it belongs in the registry, not here.

excluded.reason: MENU MECHANICS. Moving the selection is how a menu is operated. Requiring it to be reachable VIA a menu is circular — you would need a menu to move within a menu. Navigation, not an action; mutates nothing.
MENU MECHANICS. The counterpart of Up, same rationale: it drives the menu rather than being an item within one.
MENU MECHANICS. Enter is how a menu item is ACTIVATED. An Enter reachable only by activating a menu item could never be pressed the first time. It is the substrate menus run on.
MENU MECHANICS. Dismissal must remain reachable when a menu is open and possibly mis-navigated; routing escape THROUGH the surface it escapes is precisely the trap it exists to undo.
PURE FOCUS MOVEMENT. Moves focus between panes and changes no state a work-item or the factory can observe.
PURE FOCUS MOVEMENT. The reverse of Tab, same rationale.
PURE FOCUS MOVEMENT (and header panning). Walks focus across body panes or scrolls the focused header; no operator action is taken.
PURE FOCUS MOVEMENT (and header panning). The counterpart of Left, same rationale.
PURE FOCUS MOVEMENT / row activation within a pane. Structural residue explicitly named excludable by the 2026-08-03 ruling.
VIEWPORT PAGING. Scrolls the content already on screen. A menu entry for 'look further down' describes the viewport, not an operator action.
VIEWPORT PAGING. The counterpart of PageUp, same rationale.
TEXT ENTRY. Edits the search / palette query character by character. Text editing inside a field is not a menu item, and a menu cannot express per-character editing.

_inert_note: Keys the handler maps to None (Home, End, Delete, Insert, F(_), Null, CapsLock, ScrollLock, NumLock, PrintScreen, Pause, Menu, KeypadBegin, Media, Modifier) are NOT listed: they carry no operator-reachable behaviour, so there is nothing for the gate to cover. The gate treats an arm returning None as inert by construction rather than by this fixture, so a key that GAINS behaviour later stops being inert and must then be registered or argued here.
